item.title: Saudi Arabia Strikes Houthi Targets as Red Sea War Escalates
item.dc:creator: Mike Schuler
item.description: Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis said Saudi Arabia was attacking the Yemeni capital Sanaa on Tuesday after a Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city's outskirts, part of a rapidly escalating war between the sides.

item.title: Supertankers Turn From Gulf Oil Transfer Hub Amid Iran’s Attacks
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: A growing number of empty supertankers have been turning away from the Persian Gulf as escalating Iranian attacks threaten a critical transfer hub for wartime oil shipments.

item.title: Trump’s Diesel Deal Irks Allies and Is Unlikely to Reduce Prices
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: President Donald Trump’s deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heightened tensions with Ukraine — all in exchange for an outcome that experts suggest is unlikely to succeed.

item.title: 11 Missing as Drone Attacks Strike Two Ships Near NATO Waters
item.dc:creator: Mike Schuler
item.description: Eleven sailors were missing at sea on Tuesday from a ship sunk by a drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, possibly the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia's ambassador.

item.title: France Seizes Another ‘Shadow Fleet’ Tanker; Russia Decries ‘Piracy’
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: France's military was taking a tanker suspected to be part of Russia's "shadow fleet" skirting Western sanctions to Reunion island on Tuesday in what Moscow called another act of "piracy."

item.title: South Korean President Hails Arctic Container Shipping Trial, but Commercial and Sanctions Questions Remain
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung welcomed the PanStar Acro and its crew home on Tuesday after the container ship completed the country’s first round-trip commercial trial through the Arctic to Europe, hailing the voyage as a potential alternative to traditional shipping lanes even as questions remain over commercial viability and cooperation with Russia.

item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Bulgaria summoned Russia’s ambassador to Sofia after two ships were hit off the country’s coast, as concerns mount over the security of Black Sea shipping.
